description: An effect body MAY return a cleanup closure, and returning none is a first-class shape, not a degenerate one (#lzeffectvoid). docs/reactive-graph.md says `run` *may* return a cleanup that runs before each rerun and on dispose; this fixture pins what that means observably for all three body shapes, because bindings spell 'no cleanup' differently -- returning nothing in lazily-js/-rs/-py/-dart/-zig, an explicit null/nil/nullptr in lazily-cs/-kt/-go/-cpp -- and the spelling must never change the behaviour. The `effect` op's `cleanup` field selects the body: `every_run` (the default when absent) returns a cleanup from every run; `none` returns the binding's idiomatic no-cleanup form from every run; `alternate` returns a cleanup from odd-numbered runs (1st, 3rd, ...) and no cleanup from even-numbered ones, counting the run at creation as the first. Each effect reads its own cell, so every publish reruns exactly one effect and no assertion depends on the order a binding flushes sibling effects in. `cleanup_order` is cumulative from the start of the fixture. What each block catches: `bare` (none) must still rerun on every publish while nothing is ever called -- on rerun or on dispose -- which a binding that drops a cleanup-less effect's subscription, or that calls a null cleanup, fails. `tidy` (every_run) pins exactly one cleanup per rerun plus one on dispose, never more. `toggle` (alternate) is the discriminating case: a binding that only overwrites its stored cleanup when the new run returned one, without clearing the slot after calling it, re-invokes run 1's cleanup at run 3 and shows an extra `toggle` at steps[11]; a binding that keeps a stale cleanup across a none-returning run calls it again on dispose at steps[15]. The final batch proves disposal detached all three effects whatever cleanup shape they had.

expect.note: an effect whose body returns no cleanup still runs on creation
run 1 of toggle returns a cleanup; nothing has been cleaned up yet
(a) a cleanup-less effect reruns when its dependency changes, and nothing is called on the rerun
and keeps rerunning: returning no cleanup did not unsubscribe it
(b) run 1's cleanup is called exactly once, before run 2
one cleanup per rerun, never a second call of an already-called cleanup
(c) cleanup -> none: run 1's cleanup is called before run 2, and run 2 returns no cleanup
none -> cleanup: run 2 returned no cleanup, so nothing is called before run 3 -- a binding that kept run 1's already-called cleanup calls it again here
run 3's cleanup is called before run 4, which returns no cleanup
(a) disposing an effect whose last run returned no cleanup calls nothing
(b) the outstanding cleanup is called exactly once on dispose
(c) toggle's last run (run 4) returned no cleanup, so dispose calls nothing -- not run 3's cleanup a second time
disposal detached every effect whatever its cleanup shape: no rerun, no further cleanup
